data.expected: A script writes every loop contract, sized to leave room for reports.
data.observed: The model built it at about 16 KB. Its first report was rejected twice and the plan stage could not close.
data.title: Model-built Backchain contract overflowed the loop's state

data.expected: An opening leaves room for the first review report.
data.observed: Luna wrote contracts of 11.9, 12.1 and 15.7 KB against a 16 KiB state limit. Fixed with a 9,216-byte budget refused at start.
data.title: Improve openings of 12 to 16 KB

data.expected: Every Backchain loop carries the size budget.
data.observed: Only the plan stage had the budget text. The step-plan loop's first report was rejected once and the loop closed with 677 bytes spare. The fix is committed locally, not released.
data.title: Step-plan Backchain contract of 11.9 KB, one rejected report

data.expected: A plan flaw found while building goes back through the script.
data.observed: The script accepted the revise outcome, issued a new step plan, and the chain resumed. Designed behaviour.
data.title: Implement returned revise and the item was replanned once

data.expected: The model runs the printed command exactly.
data.observed: Three refused calls, each recovered in one turn. The run path is over 100 characters.
data.title: The model drops a space inside long callback paths

data.expected: The fast gate predicts the slow, deep run.
data.observed: Sonnet's plan stage took about 0.6 minutes (accept timestamps) and it never starts a Backchain loop, so the state overflow only appeared on Luna, hours in.
data.title: Sonnet passes what Luna fails

data.expected: Fewer review passes would make Luna much faster.
data.observed: They are about 16% of the time and later passes keep finding real issues. No prompt change; a metric records passes per child.
data.title: Repeat review passes are not the cost

data.expected: A grade reflects the engine, not the harness.
data.observed: The resume prompt named a bare CLI, a finished run could not be graded, and a retention check matched only headings. All fixed with tests.
data.title: The harness graded correct runs as failed

data.expected: Only credentials are refused.
data.observed: 'session token: opaque UUID' was refused twice. Descriptive values are now allowed; real secrets are still refused.
data.title: The credential check refused a plain description

data.expected: Each pass finds a material gap in the plan or is a confirmation the loop needs to close.
data.observed: Pass 1 (11 min) found three gaps: F-1 a wrong supplier direction between the page and the server, F-2 an unindexed API concurrency obligation, F-3 an omitted browser recovery requirement. It edited 14 of 20 steps: +5.8 KB, inputs 56 to 58 (one new supplier edge, one new null-origin fact). The pre-loop candidate was recovered byte-exact (digest 9e321e3d) from pass 1's audit input; the script kept no copy.
data.title: Plan loop pass 1 changed most of the graph

data.expected: A pass that reopens the loop is about the product plan.
data.observed: F-7 was a stale source label (SRC-8 authority) in Backchain's scratch metadata. The candidate digest was the same before and after (3853b978). The clean streak was already 0, so F-7 cost one extra confirming pass (pass 7, 4 to 12 min) plus its repair inside pass 5, not the whole 17 minutes. Correction of an earlier entry that said it reset the streak. No product impact seen.
data.title: Pass 5 found a gap in Backchain's own metadata and changed no plan bytes

data.evidence: until-loop receipts: trivial_streak 2 of 2; review-records candidate digests
data.expected: The closing passes are cheap next to what the earlier passes found.
data.observed: Plan passes 6 and 7 (12 and 4 min) and step-plan passes 3 and 4 (6 and 4 min) changed nothing, as the stop rule requires. Plan pass 7 exists only because F-7 kept pass 5 from being clean. It is unknown whether any clean pass ever prevented a defect.
data.title: Two clean passes close every loop and cost 26 minutes across the two loops

data.expected: A ShipLoop script checks ids, references, cycles and sinks and writes a receipt.
data.observed: The plan result says its structural status is unknown because no deterministic validation receipt exists. A duplicate step id (S20) was caught only by the model's own check before freezing.
data.title: The graph's structure is asserted by the model, not verified by a script

data.expected: ShipLoop uses the graph's order, groups and sinks to run the work.
data.observed: The plan graph has 20 steps and an empty parallel_groups list, and maps to a single item (W1). The step-plan stage then built a second 20-step graph for W1.
data.title: A 20-step graph was mapped to one work item with no parallel groups

data.expected: A fact already in the spec, the acceptance criteria, is supplied by the script, not planned again.
data.observed: Plan steps S11 to S20 and step-plan steps S8 to S17 are one 'independently confirmed' step per criterion: half of the plan graph and half of the step-plan graph. Elaboration doubled the 10-step draft to 20 (20 minutes before the first pass).
data.title: Both loops carry the same ten per-criterion verification steps

data.expected: A closed plan is revised only for what could not be seen at planning time.
data.observed: The W1 plan and test strategy were revised so SYS-PORT-09 checks the sanitized child PORT separately from its readiness probe port, after two loops and eleven reviewed passes. One instance; unknown whether the spec or sources already showed it.
data.title: The item plan was revised during build for a port check

data.expected: We know what the loops add.
data.observed: Sonnet never starts a loop and runs four cases end to end in 8 to 40 minutes; Luna spends about 4.4 hours in two loops (263 min). The models differ, so neither run says what a loop would have found on the other.
data.title: No comparison exists between a run with Backchain loops and one without

data.expected: Per-stage minutes come from the script's own timestamps.
data.observed: By accept timestamps test-strategy took 94 min and plan 196 min; the harness reports 224 and 39. The totals agree within 5 minutes (385 and 380 through plan), so only the attribution is wrong.
data.title: Harness stage minutes move time between stages

data.evidence: review-records/action-2..4-review.json; candidate digests b66d62f0, b4567c04, bfd6b9f6, 3853b978
data.expected: Each pass either changes the plan or is a confirmation the loop needs to close.
data.observed: Passes 2 to 4 (59 min) each changed one confirm clause (S2 inspect to execute, S4 inspects the dependency files, S11 made deterministic): +0.4 KB together, same ids, edges and produces. Passes 5 to 7 (33 min) changed nothing. Whether a stronger confirmation changes what gets built is the open question.
data.title: After pass 1 the plan loop only refined confirm clauses

data.expected: A fact the packet already states is planned in the draft, not found by the loop.
data.observed: Pass 1 (42 min) added rejection tests and docstrings the parent packet requires, and a style note (F-01, F-02). Pass 2 (55 min) added D3, covering README and local-skill fit and the entrypoint contract, and changed 16 existing steps, mostly inputs (F-03, F-04). Snapshots 6f971770 then 024b3dc3; passes 3 and 4 changed nothing.
data.title: Step-plan passes 1 and 2 added steps for items the parent packet already required

data.expected: Every candidate a loop checked is recoverable from the run.
data.observed: The frozen plan candidate (digest 9e321e3d in the freeze log) is no file in the run. It was recovered only because pass 1's audit input embedded a copy that hashes exactly to it. The step-plan loop kept review snapshots; the plan loop did not, and neither kept the bind-time step-plan candidate.
data.title: The script kept no snapshot of the candidate at each pass

data.expected: A plan is reviewed once by the loop that owns its convergence.
data.observed: After Backchain closed, Improve reviewed the plan again: the plan stage took 44 min after the Backchain result (about 5 min of handoff, then 3 review passes; the last reports no new defect) and the step-plan stage 24 min. Whether Improve finds what Backchain would is untested.
data.title: Each plan also gets a second whole-plan review from the mandatory Improve child

data.expected: Behaviour does not depend on the model.
data.observed: Sonnet's plan reviews run 98 to 439 bytes (battleship: 104 bytes each, 'No material finding, no edits'). Luna's are 2,352 and 2,319 bytes, each listing what was reopened and rechecked. An Improve-only arm is a weaker control on Sonnet than on Luna.
data.title: Improve's plan reviews are one line each on Sonnet and 2.3 KB each on Luna

data.expected: The script decides what runs; the model never chooses the next stage.
data.observed: The packet says the host 'may request' one Backchain action; nothing in ShipLoop requires or checks it. Luna ran two loops (263 min); all four Sonnet runs ran none: no Backchain scratch directory and no until-loop receipt, and the plan stage was accepted in 0.5 to 1.1 min.
data.title: Whether a plan gets a Backchain loop is the model's choice

data.expected: The script can tell when a plan result claims Backchain evidence.
data.observed: The 'Backchain standalone Until Loop binding:' marker the guidance asks the model to preserve is not in the plan result, its notes, its inbox copies or the step-plan result; it sits inside the cited until-loop-receipt.json. 28 of the plan result's 56 evidence refs point into a model-chosen scratch directory. Exactly one cited file in each result has the Backchain plan shape (the final candidate), but the run holds eight such files.
data.title: ShipLoop cannot tell from the plan result that a Backchain loop ran

data.expected: A plan the loop closes passes the structural check.
data.observed: Pass 1's repair added discovered step D1 (the production Node entrypoint contract) with no consumer. lib.js invariant 4 rejects both step-plan snapshots (6f971770 and 024b3dc3). Passes 2 to 4 and Improve accepted it. The plan candidates pass once packaged; raw they fail invariant 6 because the stored groups are [].
data.title: The reference validator rejects the accepted step-plan candidate

data.expected: The model follows the packet; the packet allows the whole plan/draft operation only at the plan stage.
data.observed: The step-plan caller packet names action plan, stage draft, workflow stage shiploop:step-plan, although step-plan may only request audit or revise (BACKCHAIN_NATIVE_CALLS has plan only). The 136-minute step-plan loop is off-protocol data, not a sample of the designed route. Superseded in part (2026-10-04): the packet text is not shown to be the cause, because the model chose the loop before reading it (o32).
data.title: The step-plan loop ran an operation its packet does not allow

data.evidence: git show db61a4a7; shiploop_prompts.py _backchain_guidance; shiploop_navigator.py resource list
data.expected: A packet carries only what its step may do.
data.observed: Since 1.16.0 (db61a4a7, a fix for stalled planning) the packets at spec, plan, step-plan, carry-forward and product-acceptance name six Backchain and Until Loop files (+86 KB, +40% required reading) and about 553 words of loop text, though only plan may start a whole loop. Luna opened Backchain SKILL.md ten times before the step-plan loop and read 29 whole reference files across plan and step-plan.
data.title: Backchain loop text and a six-file reading list are printed at every Backchain stage

data.expected: Planning time goes to work that changes the plan.
data.observed: Step-plan loop 136 min (23%, off-protocol), plan loop 128 (22%), Improve review loops 186 (31%), Improve opening files 35 (6%), producer stage work 107 (18%). Sonnet got the same packets and planned in 4 minutes, so packet size is not the driver; model effort and the loops are. The shares are inferred from timestamps.
data.title: Where the planning time went: 592 min for the first work item

data.expected: One rule per behaviour: screen the lenses once, read references by section.
data.observed: convergence.md asks every pass for actual reads of the applicable cards and an all-42-lens screen, while technical-lenses.md says to screen all categories once and not paste the library into every call. Each review record is 36 to 39 KB, about 60% a copied lens screen. The printed head says never read a whole reference file; convergence.md says read the card and adapter reference in full.
data.title: Per-pass rules contradict the lens index and the printed head

data.expected: Run metrics count what happened once.
data.observed: metrics.json improve_children counts each child's directory and its -bind.md file: 16 for 8 children, and 14 for the 7 children of this run. The exporter counts directories. The harness's stage minutes and per-stage turns misattribute time the same way; accept deltas are the fix.
data.title: The harness counts each Improve child twice

data.evidence: v1161-battleship-luna events.jsonl: the complete output after select-work (a 5,250 B step-plan head with no mention of Backchain), then the model's next message; docs/shiploop-i2b-trim-planning-prompts-plan-2026-10-04.md
data.expected: A decision to start a loop comes from the packet the script printed for that stage.
data.observed: The step-plan head the model received never mentions Backchain, and its next message says it is using the Backchain planning skill, before it opens the full packet. The whole plan/draft choice came from carried context (the plan-stage loop, and SKILL.md's stage-less wording), so trimming step-plan packet text can be neither credited nor blamed. One run, one model.
data.title: The step-plan loop choice predates the step-plan packet text

data.evidence: docs/experiments/shiploop-callback-failures-20261004/ (script and failures.json, reproduced byte-identical); LEARNINGS section on callback path typos
data.expected: The model copies the printed callback exactly.
data.observed: 41 failed ShipLoop or Until Loop commands in nine runs. All six inserted-space paths sit in session 2 of one resumed Luna run (3 of 52 callbacks; session 1 had 0 of 41 under the same run name), so the run-name explanation is contradicted and session age is the leading, unproven cause. Every error was repaired by the next call (one by +2), 110 s in 18.8 h, no state change. Engine change deferred; reopen when a path typo appears in any other run (R1) or one is not repaired by the next call (R2).
data.title: Callback path typos cluster in one resumed Luna session; engine change deferred

data.evidence: metrics.json shiploop_failures for the seven Claude runs; failures.json
data.expected: Run metrics count the failures of every host.
data.observed: metrics.collect reads only ACP tool_call_update events, so shiploop_failures is empty for all seven Claude runs while the same runs hold 15 failing ShipLoop or Until Loop commands and 28 to 40 refusals behind exit 0. Claude failure counts are lower bounds, and earlier journal cells reading 0 for Claude are unmeasured. Fix is a metrics item (M1) that waits for the other session's metrics.py change.
data.title: Claude failure counts are lower bounds: the harness cannot see them

data.evidence: v1161-battleship-luna: run/state.md (status blocked, stage system-test, revision 57), the system-test packet, docs/shiploop/test-strategy.md#browser-procedure-and-open-observation, result.json
data.expected: A step that needs something only a person can supply is recorded as an open item and the run continues with everything that does not depend on it (S-14).
data.observed: All five registered Node suites passed on the real candidate (16 of 16). The test strategy, written three stages earlier, had planned two required browser cases that need a person with DevTools; system-test marked itself blocked and ended on the awaiting route, after the callback refused the first blocked result with the S-14 rule and the model resubmitted blocked. Cause found by reading the packets: a stage advances only with done, and the closing paragraph of Stage readiness and completion says a required case already due and not run prevents completing the stage; the system-test duties have no open-item route (release-verify has one). The host ended its own turn after a 9.29 h resumed session: 39 accepted actions in 19.3 h; product-acceptance, release-plan, release-check and the report never ran. Sonnet's battleship runs recorded the same browser limit as an open item and passed.
data.title: The Luna run ended blocked at system-test on two human-only browser cases

data.evidence: v1161-battleship-luna result.json (plugin loaded [], process pass) against the first process's baseline row (plugin true, process false)
data.expected: A grade means the engine, not the harness: resuming a run does not change whether the plugin loaded.
data.observed: The resumed process graded plugin as failed with no plugin listed, while the first process of the same run graded it true. The resume path carries no evidence of the original install, so a resumed Codex run reads as a plugin failure. Cause not traced; the process that graded it ran the harness code from before the exporter and the regrade fix.
data.title: A resumed Codex run grades the plugin as failed

data.evidence: evidence/claude-claude-sonnet-5-5-1.19.0-hello-20261004.json and the three other hello runs (page runs hello-1161, hello-1180, hello-1190a, hello-1190b)
data.expected: A pass on the fast gate predicts a pass on a slower run, and the same trivial request costs about the same each release.
data.observed: Sonnet hello passes every time with 0 failures, but its cost read 143, 167, 194 and 254 turns ($3.30, $4.39, $5.37, $7.33) across 1.16.1, 1.18.0 and the two 1.19.0 runs. A read-only investigation did not find a release cause: the Improve text and review focus are byte-identical, 9 of 12 first-pass changes were real defects, and 73% of the repeat's extra cost was one refusal-triggered replan (o39). The environment was uncontrolled (connectors loaded in two runs, o38; a CLI update; two runs concurrent), and the same-release noise ($1.96) is larger than the release steps ($1.10, $0.98). Not shown to be release-linked; the cost of one hello per release stays on the page as context, not as a regression.
data.title: The same hello request costs more with each release

data.evidence: init events of the four hello runs (mcp_servers, tools); the one-turn probe with and without --strict-mcp-config; commit bc3046db
data.expected: A grade means the engine, not the harness: an unattended run sees only the plugin under test.
data.observed: Two of four Claude hello runs loaded 15 of the user's claude.ai connectors and 174 tools (several connected, including Interactive Brokers and Docusign) into an unattended run; two loaded none. A plain launch with --setting-sources project,local loads them; adding --strict-mcp-config loads 0 servers and 28 tools. It confounded the cost comparison (about 60k against 54k initial context) and let a model reach account connectors. Fixed: ClaudeHost passes --strict-mcp-config, pinned by a test.
data.title: Claude E2E runs loaded the user's claude.ai connectors

data.evidence: v1190-hello-sonnet-2: system-test-author result (ST-1 recorded as a shell pipeline in suite focused), the refusal, the docs-only W2 replan
data.expected: A refused result is repaired in place; the model does not add work to get past it.
data.observed: system-test-author recorded a shell pipeline as suite focused; ShipLoop refused it (could not read how many tests it ran); the model replanned with a docs-only second work item, forcing select-work, step-plan, a second run and a second system-test: about 24 calls and $1.44, 73% of that run's extra cost over its sibling. The guidance names suites focused, regression or check without defining check; only the step-plan text does. One run so far.
data.title: A refused system-test command led the model to add a second work item

data.goal: Follow docs/shiploop-backchain-validator-comparison-plan-2026-10-04.md, iterations I3 to I6: build the arm runner, pilot one case with three arms on Sonnet 5.5, screen with the pre-registered rule, then decide the loop policy.
data.title: Run the Backchain comparison, pilot first
data.why: Deciding what the loop should do needs a comparison we do not have. Track 1 compares draft, one-shot plus checker and loop on planted-defect cases; Track 2 only follows if Track 1 shows lift.

data.goal: Design and build a ShipLoop script that writes the Backchain Until Loop start contract (like improve-start), with a size guard, then verify it with a seeded Luna run.
data.title: Make a script write the Backchain loop contract
data.why: Removes model sizing from the one loop the model still builds. Verify with a unit test and a seeded Luna run at step-plan.

data.goal: Follow docs/shiploop-backchain-validator-comparison-plan-2026-10-04.md, iterations I1 and I2: a Python port of Backchain's seven invariants with parity tests against the Backchain checkout, a backchain-check verb, and a gate that validates any cited Backchain-shaped candidate at complete.
data.title: Build the Backchain graph validator (I1 and I2)
data.why: The model asserts structure in prose and the result admits there is no receipt. It will not save minutes (every saved candidate already passes); it gives a script-run check, a snapshot of each cited candidate and the parallel groups.

data.goal: Have the script emit one verification step per acceptance criterion from the spec's criteria list, so the model plans only the build steps. Measure the minutes saved in the plan and step-plan loops and whether the findings change.
data.title: Generate the per-criterion verification steps from the spec
data.why: Half of each graph is one step per acceptance criterion, planned twice by the model. The criteria list already exists.

data.goal: Decide what ShipLoop does with a Backchain graph: use its order and groups to open work items, or ask Backchain for a build plan only and stop mapping a graph to one item. Record the decision and reason in the spec, then change the expectation here to match.
data.title: Decide what the plan graph is for
data.why: A 20-step graph mapped to one item with no parallel groups is not driving anything the script can see.

data.goal: Release 1.16.2 (budget text at every Backchain stage and per-section sizes in the refusal), refresh the hosts, run the Sonnet hello gate, then verify the step-plan fix with a seeded Luna run.
data.title: Release 1.16.2 after the Luna run ends
data.why: Budget text at every Backchain stage and per-section sizes in the refusal are committed locally. A release now would break the Codex resume.

data.goal: Add a Sonnet end-to-end case with a large enough plan and context to start the Backchain loops, so the fast gate covers the size-budget path.
data.title: Add a Sonnet case that reaches the Backchain loops
data.why: Lets the fast gate catch Luna-depth defects in minutes instead of a day.

data.goal: Make ShipLoop print each callback as a copy-ready command file or short run alias, and measure whether path typos in refusals drop.
data.title: Print copy-ready callbacks
data.why: The model drops spaces when re-typing long run paths. A short alias or a command file costs a few lines.

data.goal: Add an expected-versus-observed block to every E2E result with the spec clause, the expectation, the measured value and the verdict, plus a per-loop Backchain ledger (each pass with minutes and what it changed in the candidate), and feed it to the run review page.
data.title: Have the harness write expected versus observed, and the Backchain ledger, per run
data.why: Turns this page into data instead of a summary written by hand. Where the script keeps snapshots and receipts the ledger is exact; elsewhere it is rebuilt from review-record digests.

data.goal: Compute per-stage minutes from ShipLoop's accepted and started timestamps, not from when packets were read, coordinate with that session's P1-1 reader, and add a test that pins the Luna 1.16.1 figures.
data.title: Derive stage minutes from the script's own timestamps
data.why: The harness reports 224 and 39 minutes where accept timestamps give 94 and 196. Another session's analysis (docs/shiploop-graph-engineering-comparison-2026-10-04.md, P1-1) proposes the same reader; do it there once.

data.goal: Let the Luna max battleship run finish, grade it, and write the full result, the stage timings and the carry-forward and product-acceptance Backchain ledgers into the journal.
data.title: Let the Luna run finish and journal it
data.why: It is the only run that exercises the whole chain on a deep model. Stopping loses that evidence, including the later Backchain stages.

data.goal: Plan iteration I2b, as built locally (3592b195): the Backchain loop text and resource list print only at plan; audit stages print the audit route, its resource and one status line; the restated identity and digest text and the Improve-owner text are shorter. Content and absence pins, no word or byte pins. The lens-screen change is a separate decision (I2c).
data.title: Trim the planning prompts before the comparison (I2b)
data.why: Planning prompts printed a six-file Backchain list and loop text at every Backchain stage. Cutting ineffective text while keeping every justified obligation shrinks the measured size (audit stages 688 to 301 words). It is not claimed to stop the step-plan whole loop, which the model chose before reading that packet (o32).

data.goal: Analysis done (read-only, quotes checked against source): the two rules do not literally collide. S-14 is in every packet, but a stage advances only with done, and the closing paragraph of Stage readiness and completion plus the system-test duties say an already-due required case not run prevents completing the stage; only release-verify has an open-item route. Fix, text only: add the open-item route to the system-test duties and an exception to that reference paragraph; handoff lists open items as unverified. Deferred: plan person-only cases as open items from test-strategy (phase two). Built locally; release with the next batch.
data.title: Decide what a required check that only a person can supply does to the run at system-test
data.why: The Luna 1.16.1 run planned two required browser cases that need a person with DevTools, then ended blocked at system-test after 9.3 hours and never reached product-acceptance, release-plan or the report. The spec says a step that needs a physical observation records an open item and continues with everything that does not depend on it; the testing reference says a required check without its capability stays blocked or unverified.

data.goal: Done by a read-only investigation: not a regression to fix in Improve (text identical, 9 of 12 first-pass changes warranted), and the release-linked reading is not supported (o37). The environment confound is fixed (a15). Optional, only if the owner wants it settled: an interleaved serial A/B, three 1.16.1 and three 1.19.0 hello runs on Sonnet 5.5 with the connector isolation, about $28.
data.title: Find what Improve's first pass changes in the hello runs since 1.18.0
data.why: The same hello request now costs more each release (143, 167, 194 and 254 turns). In 1.16.1 every one of the eight Improve children finished in one pass; in 1.18.0 five of eight took three passes, in the 1.19.0 runs three of eight and four of eleven. Whether those first passes make warranted changes or churn is unknown, and the work-item count also varies (one item in three runs, two in the repeat).

data.goal: ClaudeHost passes --strict-mcp-config (bc3046db, pushed, harness only). A one-turn probe showed 0 servers and 28 tools with the flag. Next runs are isolated; no release needed.
data.title: Isolate Claude E2E runs from the user's account connectors
data.why: A plain Claude launch loaded 15 claude.ai connectors and 174 tools into two of four hello runs, some connected (trading and signing services among them), which is both a safety gap for unattended runs and a confound for cost comparisons.

data.goal: Wait for a recurrence in at least one of the next runs before touching text; then add the definition of check to the system-test-author guidance, as the step-plan guidance already has it.
data.title: Define the check suite in the system-test-author guidance, only if the replan recurs
data.why: The 1.19.0 hello repeat spent about $1.44 on a replan after ShipLoop refused a shell pipeline recorded as suite focused; the guidance lists focused, regression or check but defines check only in the step-plan text (o39).

data.text: Each Backchain pass either finds a material gap in the plan or is a confirmation the loop needs to close. Time spent on a pass that finds nothing is the price of closing, and it should be small next to what the earlier passes found.
data.title: Every pass earns its time

data.text: Unique step ids, resolved references, one confirmation per produce, no cycles and every step reaching a sink are checked by a ShipLoop script that writes a receipt. The model does not assert them.
data.title: A script verifies the graph

data.text: ShipLoop uses the plan graph's order, groups and sinks to open work items and to know when a plan is satisfied. A graph that is only mapped to one item is not being used.
data.title: The script uses the graph to run the work

data.text: A fact already in the spec, such as the list of acceptance criteria, is not derived again by the model in each loop. The script supplies it and the loops plan only what is new.
data.title: Planning is not repeated for the same facts

data.text: When Backchain closes a plan, a revise outcome during the build is for what could not be seen at planning time, not for what the spec and sources already showed.
data.title: A closed plan is not revised for visible gaps

data.text: The model never chooses the next stage. It does the step in the packet and calls back.
data.title: The script owns the flow

data.text: Improve, test and quality loop contracts are written by ShipLoop. A model should never size or build one.
data.title: The script writes every loop contract

data.text: The model follows the printed packet and commands exactly.
data.title: The packet is the only instruction

data.text: Each turn does one stage's work and ends with the exact callback.
data.title: One step, then call back

data.text: Findings are committed with the work, and a grade means the engine, not the harness.
data.title: Evidence is trustworthy and in the repo

data.text: A pass on the fast gate should predict a pass on a slower, deeper model.
data.title: Behaviour does not depend on the model

data.text: Expectations for the dependency-planning loop: what each pass should earn, who checks the graph, whether the script uses it, and whether planning is repeated.
data.title: What we expect of Backchain

data.text: Mark each as holds, bent or broken; select it again to mark it unjudged. Revise the wording when we learn the principle itself was wrong or incomplete. What we saw is filled in from the observations tagged to it.
data.title: Principles

revs.from: A Python port of Backchain's seven invariants agrees with the Backchain checkout's reference validator on every fixture there and on single-edit mutations of them: the same ok, the same failing invariant numbers and the same parallel groups. It reports ok for the three saved Luna candidates.
revs.reason: Adversarial review of the plan, checked against the run on 2026-10-04: the reference validator rejects the accepted step-plan candidate on invariant 4, so 'ok for the three saved candidates' was wrong.
